peaks.notes: Method: pdftotext -layout on all four PDFs; page attribution via form-feed page breaks plus printed footers (6-xx / 5-xx for JICA 2012, A4-xx appendix pages for JICA 2019, 623-628 and 23-32 for the two IOE papers). Key negatives verified by exhaustive grep: (a) JICA 2012 Vol02 never states the clock windows of the two 3-hour intersection-count periods; (b) JICA 2019 Vol02 contains no numeric signal phase/green-time values as text — only the A4-12 methodology sentence (values may exist inside Figure 4.2 images, not extractable); (c) Thapathali 2023 never prints clock times for its peak hours. Bonus nearby fact if useful: Thapathali 2023 Table 5 (printed p. 28) gives police-assigned peak-hour phase timings P1-P5 per day (e.g. Day1: 74/121/73/57/116 s, sum 441 s; Day4: 9/25/17/12/27 s, sum 90 s). Also note the JICA 2012 internal contradiction on p. 6-35: Table 6.2.12 header says evening 16:00-17:00 while Table 6.2.13 on the same page says Evening Peak(17:00-18:00). Working text files kept in the session scratchpad (jica2012v2.txt, jica2019v2.txt, maitighar2017.txt, thapathali2023.txt).

zones.notes:
METHOD: The Appendix 1.1.1 table (pp. AP 1-1 to AP 1-4 = PDF pages 4-7 of vol04) is stored as raster page images with no extractable text, so pages were rendered with pdftoppm (150 dpi) and transcribed visually; rendered pages kept at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-isubash-Developer-mod/2f653dbb-0bd3-47a6-ae97-d65cdb5ba364/scratchpad/vol04zone-04..07.png. Quotes for zone rows are transcriptions from those page images, not text-layer extractions. All 50 small zones (101-119, 201-202, 301-306, 401-404, 501-502, 601-610, 701-704, 801-803) are covered; count matches Table 5.1.4 (19+2+6+4+2+10+4+3 = 50).

EXTERNAL ZONES: Codes 900/901 are NOT FOUND in the Appendix 1.1.1 zone code table. They appear only in OD tables: 901 as a destination-only column in the Person Trip OD Table (Appendix 1.1.4, AP 1-5/1-6; column total 4,060, no 901 origin row), and 900 as origin row + destination column in the Vehicle OD tables (Appendix 1.2.6). The tables print no name for 900/901; vol02 sec 6.2(6) describes boundary movement (~24,000 veh/day, Table 6.2.3: Eastern Area Outside, Western Area Outside, Lalitpur South, India) but does not explicitly label these as zone 900/901 — that linkage is NOT stated in the files.

CORRIDOR CAVEAT: For municipal zones the Ward/VDC column prints only ward numbers — no locality names (Tripureshwor, Baneshwor, Koteshwor etc. are never mapped to wards anywhere in vol01/vol02/vol04 text). The on_corridor flags therefore rest on geographic position in Figure 5.1.1 Zoning Map (vol02, p. 5-4 = PDF p.4; high-res crop at scratchpad/crop-center.png): zone 108 fronts the Bagmati between 109 and 107 (Tripureshwor-Thapathali-Maitighar stretch); 107 sits east of 108 on the axis alignment (New Baneshwor; vol04 Appendix 1.2.3 lists 'G. New Baneshwor Intersection' and 'E. Thapathali Intersection' as survey points but without zone numbers); 119 is the southeast KMC zone at the river bend (Koteshwor; 'H. Koteshwor Intersection' in Appendix 1.2.3); 502 is the Thimi zone across the boundary at Jadibuti; 109 (Teku), 110 (Kalimati per task example), 114 (city core per task example) and 301 (Lalitpur across the Thapathali bridge) border the axis. Treat yes-flags on 109/110/114/301/502 as 'adjacent' and 107/108/119 as 'on'. Borderline cases marked no: 801 (BALKOT is across the Bagmati from the Koteshwor-Jadibuti stretch), 704 (TIKATHALI across the river to the south), 116/118 (Anamnagar/Putalisadak-area wards possibly touching the Maitighar-Baneshwor road, but no file evidence of ward localities). Zone-system description sourced from vol02 sec 5.1.3/Table 5.1.4 (vol01 contains only TOC references to zoning; the 86-zone assignment system body is in a volume not examined here, likely vol03).
